walkthroughs.body_html:
The 1845-49 Famine killed 1 million in Ireland and pushed 1 million more abroad.

By 1861 over 600,000 Irish-born people lived in Britain. They dug canals and railways as navvies, often faced anti-Catholic prejudice and the slur 'No Irish Need Apply'.

After Tsar Alexander II was assassinated in 1881, pogroms swept the Russian Empire.

About 150,000 Jews settled in Britain by 1914, mostly in London's East End. They worked in tailoring shops in Whitechapel and built synagogues, schools and Yiddish theatres.

Lascars — sailors from India, Yemen and Somalia — worked British steamships.

Some settled in dockland communities in Cardiff, Liverpool and South Shields. In 1905 anti-Jewish lobbying led to the Aliens Act — Britain's first major immigration control.
